A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Fourier Learning Machines study. All 35 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original FLM experiments on four PDEs and optimal control problems in Section 5, plus ETTh1 imputation results and hyperparameter experiments in Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original PDE, optimal control, imputation and hyperparameter results, including their numerical tables and plots.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same cosine-activated FLM architecture, trainable frequencies, amplitudes and phases, and sign patterns prescribed by the m-Lexi Sign Matrix. Section 5's training objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same heat, Poisson, generalized Black–Scholes and Burgers PDEs, three- and five-strategy optimal control scenarios, and ETTh1 oil-temperature imputation at 10% and 50% missingness.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Appendix C retain identical task-specific SIREN and vanilla-network comparator rows. The PMP-based control reference and the imputation comparator rows in Table 3 also match.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C retain the same sampling procedures, model sizes, optimizers, training budgets, stopping criteria and metrics. The ETTh1 chronological training/validation/test split remains 60%/20%/20%.

E4.justification: Figure 9's analysis of approximation error versus the number of FLM subnetworks and Appendix C's hyperparameter analyses are unchanged. The solution-error plots and optimal control case studies also match.

E5.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same reporting over 10 runs with different seeds, including means and standard deviations. The hierarchical statistical tests for PDE hyperparameter selection are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, FLM's heat-equation MSE remains 6.24e-8 in Table 2a, and its ETTh1 MAEs remain 0.57 and 0.66 at 10% and 50% missingness in Table 3.

T1.justification: The definitions and mathematical derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A are unchanged, including the m-Lexi Sign Matrix and the relationships between separable Fourier coefficients and phase-shifted cosine parameters.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about representing complete separable Fourier bases through an MLP-like architecture and achieving competitive PDE and optimal control performance.

C2.justification: The discussions of exponential growth with input dimension, difficulties with Burgers discontinuities, initialization questions and preliminary imputation performance remain unchanged in Section 4, Section 5 and Appendix B.

D1.justification: Initialization, implementation and hyperparameter disclosures in Section 5 and Appendices B–C are identical. The new publication notice adds citation guidance, without adding implementation or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. The new TMLR notice identifies the published version of this same work; it does not add prior research or revise the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a two-line publication and citation notice beneath the author affiliations and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The existing prose, terminology and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The notice reflows pages 1–7: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, and Section 3 begins on page 7 instead of page 6. Figure and table content is unchanged; pages 8–35 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 adds publication citation guidance and causes limited opening-page reflow. The scientific argument, results, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged, while the layout shifts leave readability essentially intact. This bibliographic update produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
